chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the menstruating woman who hands the man the water. He said: 'Some of the wives of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) would pour water for him while they were menstruating, and they would hand him the prayer-mat.'

key_terms.الْخُمْرَةَ: The prayer-mat (small mat used for prayer)

ai.seo_question: Is a menstruating woman considered ritually impure (najisa) in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the Shia doctrine of 'taharat al-ha'id' (the purity of the menstruating woman), refuting the view that menstrual blood renders her entirely impure (najis al-dam) in a way that prohibits physical contact. By citing the practice of the Prophet's wives pouring water and handing him items, it establishes that their bodily fluids and general state were compatible with the Prophet's purity, thereby validating their daily interactions. This serves as a foundational textual evidence for the permissibility of menstruating women performing general acts of worship and interacting with others without requiring full ritual washing (ghusl) for every touch.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the menstruating woman fetching the water for the man’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It was so that some of the wives of the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> would pour the water for him<sup>saww</sup>, and she would be menstruating, and she would fetch the prayer-mat for him<sup>saww</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “I once asked abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

about the woman who during her Hayd (menses) brings water for the man. He (the Imam) said, ‘Wives of the Holy prophet, would pour water on him during their experiencing Hayd (menses) and furnish for him prayer mat.”’
